source.snippet: I work for a small MSP. Most of the work can be done from home but sometimes my boss asks me to go to client sites. Usually I get no notice about this... if it's planned maintenance or an upgrade, I think me getting notice would benefit all parties involved.

problem_statement: MSP technicians and field service workers lack a lightweight scheduling and advance-notice tool that coordinates planned on-site visits between managers and technicians, resulting in last-minute dispatches that disrupt personal and professional planning.
target_segment: Small to mid-sized MSPs and field service companies with 2–20 technicians who manage client site visits without a formal scheduling system.
notes: MSPs are known paying buyers for tooling (ConnectWise, Autotask). The pain is operational inefficiency with direct cost implications (technician time, driving costs). Score 6 with 3 comments suggests relatable problem. A focused lightweight scheduling/notification layer for MSPs too small for full PSA suites could have a clear buyer.
